pages.name: Ideological Camps: Iconoclasts, Idealists, and Individualists

text.content:
Though Clan @UUID[Compendium.vtmlarp.clans.JournalEntry.ZFYurbvAHfaRguYI]{Brujah} has no formal doctrine, individual @UUID[Compendium.vtmlarp.clans.JournalEntry.ZFYurbvAHfaRguYI]{Brujah} and clan observers commonly sort the Rabble's temperaments into three loose camps. These are informal self-descriptions and social reputations rather than organized factions with membership rolls, but Storytellers may use them to color a @UUID[Compendium.vtmlarp.clans.JournalEntry.ZFYurbvAHfaRguYI]{Brujah} character's outlook, reputation among clanmates, and the kind of causes she gravitates toward.

Iconoclasts: The most common camp among modern Brujah, especially the young. Iconoclasts are the bomb-throwing rebels, quick to rally to any cause that promises change and quick to violence in its name. Many gravitate to anarch factions, gangs, and street movements. They are often short-sighted and heedless of consequence, but their passion and conviction are unmatched—ironically, they need the very institutions (the @UUID[Compendium.vtmlarp.sects.JournalEntry.fc464242d84d4e34]{Camarilla} foremost among them) that they rage against, since without an establishment to defy, an iconoclast has nothing to rebel against.

Idealists: The camp of elders and ancillae who have grown past the rambunctious neonate stage. Idealists study the past for guidance, weigh consequences, and prefer discussing an idea to throwing a trash can through a window—though they are just as capable of blood-rage as any Brujah, and just as devoted to change; they simply believe in achieving it deliberately. Brujah primogen often embody this archetype. Idealists are sometimes derided by iconoclasts as sellouts or as elders manipulating the young for their own ends.

Individualists: A less commonly recognized third camp, existing between the poles of iconoclasm and idealism. An individualist pursues change for the good of others as she defines it, but neither demands that others follow her lead nor rushes headlong into destruction; she simply charts her own course and lets others join if they wish. Some Brujah dismiss the term as an affectation, since the moment an individualist cares whether others follow her, she becomes an idealist by another name.

These distinctions are entirely behavioral rather than political; a Brujah is free to call herself whatever she likes, and just as many Rabble reject the whole taxonomy as pretentious nonsense used by "verbose Brujah" to feel superior to their clanmates.

The @UUID[Compendium.vtmlarp.clans.JournalEntry.ZFYurbvAHfaRguYI]{Brujah}'s closest equivalent to a formal institution is the rant, a clan gathering that can range from an informal bull session to a highly structured convocation, depending on who calls it and who attends. Anyone may call a rant; the only real difficulty is ensuring people show up, and whoever organizes one is responsible for arrangements such as venue, security, and feeding (hungry @UUID[Compendium.vtmlarp.clans.JournalEntry.ZFYurbvAHfaRguYI]{Brujah} at a rant are not known for their patience or discretion). Most rants follow a stage-and-audience model where anyone may speak, though the loudest, oldest, or most physically intimidating attendees tend to dominate the floor.

Rants occur at wildly different frequencies from city to city—some cities see none in a given year, while a few @UUID[Compendium.vtmlarp.clans.JournalEntry.ZFYurbvAHfaRguYI]{Brujah} have made a tradition of hosting an annual or once-a-decade gala rant (a solstice rant in Prague draws Eastern European Rabble every year; a Texas rant coincides annually with the Burning Man festival). Storytellers can use the rant as a recurring set piece: a venue where local (and sometimes traveling) Brujah air grievances, settle disputes, plan action, or simply blow off steam, with the ever-present risk that tempers boil over into brawls, riots, or worse.

Common varieties of rant include:

Policy Rants: Called to galvanize local Brujah toward a common, usually temporary, cause—for example, uniting to block an unwanted appointment or oppose a prince's overreach. A famous (if apocryphal) example holds that the Brujah of London once forced Prince Mithras to abandon plans for a second @UUID[Compendium.vtmlarp.clans.JournalEntry.OpCOs3PLjmtl0QVu]{Ventrue} primogen seat by threatening collective violence against any Kindred who accepted the position.

Debates: The near-exclusive purview of elders and intellectuals, debates argue an issue for its own sake through formal examination and cross-examination, sometimes over the course of several nights or weeks, and may lead into a policy rant afterward. Debates rarely turn violent, though exceptions occur.

Prestige Rants: Recognize (and often mock) the achievements of individual Brujah. These are frequently invitation-only, and declining an invitation invites public derision worse than simply attending and enduring the ribbing. Formats range from mock "coming out" parties to elaborate formal processions in which the honoree recounts her deeds.

Rally Rants: Straightforward affairs meant to whip local Brujah into a fervor before turning them loose on a target, whether a rival gang, a @UUID[Compendium.vtmlarp.sects.JournalEntry.6868ee8c357f4b73]{Sabbat} incursion, or a mortal institution. Rally rants often result in significant property damage and civil unrest.

Spite Rants: Rare and brutal, spite rants exist solely to punish a Kindred who has transgressed against the clan, a specific brood, or a local power structure. Punishments can range from a beating to Final Death, meted out by an incensed mob of neonates and ancillae.

Where rants address business, raves are @UUID[Compendium.vtmlarp.clans.JournalEntry.ZFYurbvAHfaRguYI]{Brujah} at play. A relatively recent institution (the term and format emerged alongside the mortal rave scene of the 1980s-90s), @UUID[Compendium.vtmlarp.clans.JournalEntry.ZFYurbvAHfaRguYI]{Brujah} raves are large, hedonistic parties open to all Kindred but overwhelmingly organized and attended by the Rabble. A rave typically precedes or follows a rant in the same city, since throwing a party before a scheduled business gathering tends to mean the business never actually gets conducted.

Raves function as neutral ground: @UUID[Compendium.vtmlarp.clans.JournalEntry.ZFYurbvAHfaRguYI]{Brujah} who might otherwise be at each other's throats over territory or ideology can meet, catch up, and blow off steam without it necessarily being read as an act of aggression. Brawls at raves are common but usually good-natured or competitive rather than lethal, though outsiders unfamiliar with Brujah roughhousing sometimes escalate a friendly scuffle into a real fight by misreading the situation. Mortal guests, drugs, alcohol, and casual feeding are all standard features; some young Kindred openly refer to the dance floor as a "buffet." At least one pair of Brujah promoters is known for running a recurring mobile rave circuit through cities as varied as Tel Aviv, Prague, Oslo, Sydney, New York, São Paulo, San Francisco, Athens, Budapest, Buenos Aires, Ibiza, Tokyo, and Hong Kong.

Raves also serve a ceremonial function: an elaborate rave is a common (if not universal) venue for the ritual release of a childe from her sire's Accounting (see the Tradition of Progeny), staged anywhere from a raucous multi-night debauch to a solemn, reserved procession, depending on the sire's temperament.

Few @UUID[Compendium.vtmlarp.clans.JournalEntry.ZFYurbvAHfaRguYI]{Brujah} hold titled positions within the @UUID[Compendium.vtmlarp.sects.JournalEntry.fc464242d84d4e34]{Camarilla}, and the clan's relationship to those who do is often uneasy—but certain offices see a disproportionate number of Rabble occupants, each shaped by the clan's particular temperament.

Prince: Vanishingly rare. Other clans consider @UUID[Compendium.vtmlarp.clans.JournalEntry.ZFYurbvAHfaRguYI]{Brujah} too capricious or emotional for the long-term stability the office demands, and most @UUID[Compendium.vtmlarp.clans.JournalEntry.ZFYurbvAHfaRguYI]{Brujah} lack the patience for the tedium of the position. European Brujah princes (more often cast in the idealist mold) hold their seats longer than the few found in the New World; the Grand Duchy of Luxembourg is a notable example of a century-long Brujah princedom.

Primogen: The clan's most visible seat of influence in city politics. Because no individual Brujah expects a primogen to represent some unified clan agenda, a Brujah primogen is largely free to pursue his own ends without his "constituents" objecting—so long as he doesn't earn open hostility, which can see him deposed or undercut by younger Brujah appealing directly to the prince. In practice, the primogen's chief function is to act as Devil's Advocate to the other primogen, questioning their motives and methods to keep them off balance, effectively serving as a Socratic check on the council and the prince alike.

Sheriff: The office most commonly held by Brujah in the @UUID[Compendium.vtmlarp.sects.JournalEntry.fc464242d84d4e34]{Camarilla}. Physical prowess, force of personality, and a taste for direct enforcement suit the position naturally; in many cities the sheriff volunteers his clan affiliation as a credential in itself.

Scourge: Also frequently a Brujah posting given its physical demands, though the attitude differs sharply from the sheriff's dutiful enforcement. A scourge's sole task is killing Kindred who violate the Traditions, and killing grows easier (and more casually rationalized) the longer one holds the office—long-tenured scourges are frequently described as cold, alien, or outright sadistic.

Harpy: Brujah harpies combine the Kindred's usual vicious social gamesmanship with the clan's passion and bluntness, making them feared rather than merely catty. They are less susceptible to simple flattery than harpies of other clans, either because they genuinely do not care what others think or because their unconventional tastes have themselves become the fashionable standard to chase.

The overwhelming majority of Brujah in @UUID[Compendium.vtmlarp.sects.JournalEntry.fc464242d84d4e34]{Camarilla} cities hold no title at all, working instead through the streets, gangs, and mortal contacts that other clans overlook.

The @UUID[Compendium.vtmlarp.clans.JournalEntry.ZFYurbvAHfaRguYI]{Brujah} antitribu emerged from the same sire-childe grievances that produced the Anarch Revolt and the founding of the @UUID[Compendium.vtmlarp.sects.JournalEntry.6868ee8c357f4b73]{Sabbat}. Unlike their @UUID[Compendium.vtmlarp.sects.JournalEntry.fc464242d84d4e34]{Camarilla}-affiliated kin, the antitribu feel no particular obligation to observe the Traditions except where convenient, and cities under heavy @UUID[Compendium.vtmlarp.sects.JournalEntry.6868ee8c357f4b73]{Sabbat} influence give them freer rein to indulge their vampiric viciousness without the social camouflage the @UUID[Compendium.vtmlarp.sects.JournalEntry.fc464242d84d4e34]{Camarilla} demands.

Where @UUID[Compendium.vtmlarp.sects.JournalEntry.fc464242d84d4e34]{Camarilla} @UUID[Compendium.vtmlarp.clans.JournalEntry.ZFYurbvAHfaRguYI]{Brujah} splinter into countless individual causes, the @UUID[Compendium.vtmlarp.sects.JournalEntry.6868ee8c357f4b73]{Sabbat}'s @UUID[Compendium.vtmlarp.clans.JournalEntry.ZFYurbvAHfaRguYI]{Brujah} cause has largely narrowed to a single unifying focus: the Sabbat itself. Antitribu are said to be gaining greater standing among the sect's traditional @UUID[Compendium.vtmlarp.clans.JournalEntry.nyOuQ8xvZEiNEJbM]{Tzimisce} and @UUID[Compendium.vtmlarp.clans.JournalEntry.phgt6OMwTAoAaKfR]{Lasombra} leadership, with tales circulating of Brujah-masterminded crusades, assassinations, and battles undertaken on the Sabbat's behalf. In practice, the methodology of Camarilla and Sabbat Brujah is nearly indistinguishable—frenzied violence, casual predation, ruthless enforcement of whatever order they serve—and the only reliable difference is which banner they claim to fight under.

Rumors also persist of an entirely separate, secret Brujah bloodline predating Troile—the so-called @UUID[Compendium.vtmlarp.clans.JournalEntry.4795a736271143af]{True Brujah}—said to be dispassionate rather than wrathful and linked by some to the shadowy Black Hand within the Sabbat. No verified account of a @UUID[Compendium.vtmlarp.clans.JournalEntry.4795a736271143af]{True Brujah} exists; the rumors remain unconfirmed hearsay even among Kindred historians.
